quotes.text: Learn how to accept iDEAL | Wero, a common payment method in the Netherlands.
This article has multiple variants. Fetch one of the following URLs to view specific content for your use case:

old_evidence.text: iDEAL | Wero (formerly iDEAL) is a [single use](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-methods.md#usage) payment method where customers are required to [authenticate](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-methods.md#customer-actions) their payment.
iDEAL | Wero doesn’t have a minimum charge amount, so the payment `amount` value can be as low as 1.

We recommend relying on Stripe.js to handle iDEAL | Wero redirects and payments with `confirmIdealPayment`. However, you can also complete the payment on your server and manually redirect your customer.

findings: Semantic raw delta: November is a 20-line variant index naming Checkout, Elements Checkout Sessions API, Elements Payment Intents API, iOS, Android and React Native (new raw lines 5-20; diff lines 3-19 and 1498-1505). The matched May full guide had Checkout, iOS, Android, React Native and an undivided Elements section (old raw lines 8-10, 126-132, 346-352, 572-578 and 860-866). The split Elements labels improve navigation but do not prove a newly added integration or changed runtime behavior.

Baseline summary accuracy: the current source says Checkout all modes and no minimum charge amount without their old-guide scope (source lines 13, 19 and 37). The old guide shows hosted and full embedded Checkout examples (old raw lines 53-103), Checkout payment/setup/subscription compatibility and EUR line items (old raw lines 22-38), but no exhaustive all-modes guarantee. The no-minimum statement is explicit for PaymentIntent creation with amount as low as 1 minor unit (old raw lines 225-245, 420-440, 652-672 and 883-885), not a tested checkout-wide rule.

Baseline summary accuracy: source line 36 asserts a legacy idealBank Element plus stripe.confirmIdealPayment and links it to server-side manual redirect. The old guide's actual Elements flow uses Payment Element with stripe.confirmPayment (old raw lines 996-1045 and 1146-1163); the manual redirect section merely recommends confirmIdealPayment before showing createPaymentMethod, server PaymentIntent confirmation, requires_action/redirect_to_url and browser redirect (old raw lines 1384-1413 and 1471-1478). No idealBank Element is documented in the complete pinned old or new raw. Remove that unsupported combined claim rather than treating it as a November deprecation.

Material dated prerequisites and outcomes omitted from the mapped summary include iDEAL Terms of Service compliance (old raw lines 18-20, 132-134 and 864-868), EUR Checkout line items (old raw lines 24-38), separate hosted success_url versus embedded return_url examples (old raw lines 53-103), and confirmation-versus-success distinction. Test authorization moves PaymentIntent requires_action to succeeded while test failure moves to requires_payment_method (old raw lines 302-307); return-page code checks succeeded, processing and requires_payment_method (old raw lines 1242-1295); post-payment webhook guidance warns against relying on client callbacks (old raw lines 1366-1370).
historical_claims_to_preserve: May 3, 2026 guide: iDEAL | Wero single-use bank-authenticated redirect, compliance with linked iDEAL Terms, EUR Checkout compatibility, payment/setup/subscription mode support and EUR line items (old raw lines 18-38). The November index supplies no refreshed eligibility or compliance evidence (new raw lines 5-20).

May guide: iOS STPPaymentHandler, Android PaymentLauncher, React Native confirmPayment and custom URL scheme/SDK callback for returning from bank redirect; universal links are not supported in the React Native guidance (old raw lines 263-300, 464-525, 720-751 and 779-839). Dated Android 23.5.0 and Stripe.js dahlia examples do not establish current version requirements (old raw lines 389-396 and 1008-1016).

May guide: 14-bank reference, 180-day refund period and no dispute process in Checkout section (old raw lines 114-118, 327-344, 553-570, 841-858 and 1480-1497). This is dated reference, not an account outcome or bank-availability test.

May guide: sandbox authorize/fail buttons and PaymentIntent states, status verification on return, and payment_intent.succeeded webhook for completed payments rather than relying on client callbacks (old raw lines 302-313, 1242-1295 and 1359-1370).
conflicts: Current source line 36 combines idealBank, confirmIdealPayment and server-side manual redirect as though the pinned guide demonstrated one supported flow. The old Payment Element flow is confirmPayment (old raw lines 996-1045 and 1146-1163); the separate server redirect example creates a PaymentMethod and confirms a PaymentIntent (old raw lines 1384-1413). No idealBank evidence appears in the complete paired raw; this is a baseline source error.

Current source lines 13 and 37 state all Checkout modes and no minimum generally. Old raw lines 53-103 demonstrate two Checkout page modes, while the no-minimum statement is tied to PaymentIntent creation at old raw lines 225-231 and 883-885. Narrow these statements and avoid extrapolating from examples.

Related concept wiki/concepts/stripe-ideal.md lines 31 and 44 repeats a broad no-minimum Checkout integration phrase. The source correction should keep the PaymentIntent amount qualification visible in reciprocal routing; no November variant content settles a universal Checkout minimum (new raw lines 9-20).
unresolved_questions: The six November variant destinations were not fetched in the approved review packet (new raw lines 11-20). Current variant behavior, availability, SDK versions and the meaning of newly split Elements links remain unverified.

source_assessments.reason: The new capture only changes navigation, but the existing summary contains unsupported and overbroad claims that need a source correction. No new current integration behavior follows from the short index.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/ideal/accept-a-payment, the complete November capture establishes a six-destination iDEAL | Wero navigation index for Checkout, Elements through Checkout Sessions or Payment Intents, iOS, Android and React Native (new raw lines 5-20). The May full guide describes a single-use, bank-authenticated EUR redirect method and requires compliance with linked iDEAL Terms; Checkout compatibility lists payment, setup and subscription modes with EUR line items, while hosted and embedded examples use different return destinations (old raw lines 18-38 and 53-103). Native and Elements paths create a server PaymentIntent and pass its client secret to the client for confirmation, with full-name collection in mobile examples (old raw lines 225-276, 420-481, 652-722 and 883-927). Test success and failure lead to distinct Intent states, and browser return is not success without status verification or payment_intent.succeeded evidence (old raw lines 302-313 and 1242-1295). The mapped source-stripe-ideal-accept-payment.md preserves much of the May routing but overstates all Checkout modes and a universal minimum, and asserts an undocumented idealBank Element (current source lines 13-37).
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/ideal/accept-a-payment, the November raw is presentation/navigation: its Elements route now names Checkout Sessions and Payment Intents separately, but its target pages were not captured and no behavioral addition or deprecation is proven (new raw lines 9-20; old raw lines 860-866). source-stripe-ideal-accept-payment.md should retain May-dated EUR, mode support, no-minimum PaymentIntent statement, 14-bank table, sandbox states, linked iDEAL Terms requirement, and webhook/status outcome boundaries (old raw lines 18-38, 225-231, 302-344 and 1242-1370), while removing the unsupported idealBank assertion and narrowing Checkout all-modes wording (current source lines 13-37). The related stripe-ideal concept repeats the broad no-minimum wording and needs a reciprocal qualification (wiki/concepts/stripe-ideal.md lines 31 and 44). Historical iOS, Android, React Native and dahlia samples remain dated; a test button, server Intent, client callback or return URL cannot establish current eligibility, settlement or a successful payment.
